note: Substrate-aware fertilization for the Daily Plan Engine. Suppresses feeding while the MG slow-release mix is active; when due, recommends a specific amendment that is ACTUALLY in inventory, by crop+stage+need, with the default application method. Hard well-water aware.

substrate.mix: Miracle-Gro 3-6 month slow-release potting mix + 10-20% perlite (+ sometimes 10% cow manure)
substrate.rationale: MG mix has built-in slow-release fertilizer feeding ~3-6 months; cow manure adds slow N. Feeding on top of fresh mix risks salt burn / excess foliage / poor fruiting. Hold routine feeding until the mix tapers.

implications: Hard water (high Ca/Mg/bicarbonate) slowly raises root-zone pH -> micronutrient (Fe/Mn) lockout, worst for acid-lovers (blueberry).
Mg is usually already present -> Epsom salt rarely needed; apply ONLY on visible Mg deficiency, not routinely.
For acid-lovers (blueberry) prefer rainwater / periodic acidification; kelp helps chelate micronutrients.
Periodic plain-water flush of containers reduces salt buildup from hard water + slow-release mix.

establishment_0_2wk.msg: Just potted — let roots establish. No N feed. Kelp (sprayer) optional for transplant stress; Mykos belongs at the transplant itself.

mg_active_3_12wk.msg: MG mix is actively feeding. No routine fertilizer. Targeted only: Epsom for visible Mg deficiency, gypsum for blossom-end rot. Kelp (sprayer) optional.

mg_tapering_13_24wk.msg: Mix tapering — begin light feeding for heavy/fruiting feeders.

needs_feed_24wk_plus.msg: Mix is spent — feed on the crop's regular cadence.

kelp.use: transplant stress, micronutrients, gentle low-N support; safe any phase

veg_feed.use: vegetative/leafy growth feed once mix tapers; the N-weighted liquid (stands in for 20-20-20)

fruiting_feed.use: fruiting/flowering crops (peppers, tomatoes, cucurbits) once mix tapers

castings.use: gentle all-purpose + microbial top-dress; safe any phase, won't burn

mycorrhizal_at_transplant.apply: in planting hole at transplant (root contact)
mycorrhizal_at_transplant.use: transplant only — root inoculant; not a top-dress later

epsom.use: ONLY on visible Mg deficiency (interveinal yellowing on older leaves); hard water already Mg-rich so rarely needed

gypsum.use: calcium for blossom-end-rot prevention (tomato/pepper) without changing pH

crop_stage_recommendation.fruiting_or_flowering: fruiting_feed (Tomato-Tone 3-4-6) once tapering; kelp sprayer optional anytime; gypsum if BER appears
crop_stage_recommendation.vegetative_leafy: veg_feed (Grow Big 6-4-4, sprayer) once tapering; castings top-dress anytime
crop_stage_recommendation.transplant_new: mycorrhizal at the transplant + kelp (sprayer) for establishment; no N
crop_stage_recommendation.acid_lover_blueberry: NEEDS acidic fertilizer (e.g. Holly-Tone — NOT in inventory, flag to acquire); use rainwater not hard well water; kelp ok
crop_stage_recommendation.herbs_mediterranean: minimal feeding ever; castings only; never force with N

inventory_gaps_flagged: No straight 20-20-20 in inventory — FoxFarm Grow Big 6-4-4 fills the vegetative liquid-feed role.
The 'MG all-purpose shake-on (fruiting-weighted)' Dave mentioned is NOT itemized in Inventory — add it if on hand (Espoma Tomato-Tone 3-4-6 currently covers the fruiting granular role).
